newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT - Teva 1996 estimate cut.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Teva 1996 estimate cut.

text.p: Lehman Brothers said it was cutting its full-year earnings per share estimate for Teva Pharmaceutical Industries but was maintaining its 1-Buy recommendation for Israel's largest drug company.

"We are trimming our full-year 1996 EPS estimate to $1.38 (from $1.54) to more conservatively reflect the commercial launch timing of multiple sclerosis drug Copaxone, which we assume will occur in early first quarter 1997; our 1997 EPS estimate remains $3.00," Lehman analyst Richard Silver said in a report.
Last year the company earned $1.23 per share.
Although the revised 1996 estimate assumes no contribution from Copaxone, Lehman expects the drug to get marketing clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration by year end.

Teva, which also trades in Tel Aviv, will report third-quarter earnings on November 11. Lehman estimates the company will report EPS of $0.35 against $0.32 a year earlier. The results reflect the U.S. launch of a generic version of Klonopin as well as acquisition-related cost savings.

"Acquisitions coupled with two major new generic drug introductions strengthen the solid, diversified base business, contrary to recent trends of other companies with U.S. generic presence," the report said.
"With Teva shares trading at only 14 times our 1997 estimate, we see opportunity for significant capital appreciation in 1997, as Teva's growth rate dramatically accelerates during the next year."
Lehman's price target for the next 12-18 months remains $70 a share compared with its current price of $40-7/8.
